newsitem.title: GERMANY: WALL STREET SLIDE PUTS PRESSURE ON GERMAN SHARES.
newsitem.headline: WALL STREET SLIDE PUTS PRESSURE ON GERMAN SHARES.

text.p: German IBIS DAX index fell over 2.40 percent in afternoon electronic trade after the dollar lost ground against the mark on the back of sterling, and Wall Street fell 1.24 percent in early trade.
"I don't know why it is down so much is the honest answer. The dollar is down a lot because of sterling, and the yen is up 1.25 on the dollar, but the situation is overdone," a trader said.
At 1345 GMT the IBIS DAX index was down 106.45 points, or 2.40 percent, at 4,321.63 points, while the September DAX future contract was down 101 points at 4,344.

German shares ran for cover when the dollar fell against the mark earlier in the afternoon, but regained some lost ground in the run up to the opening of the Dow Jones Industrial index across the Atlantic.
A lower overnight close on Wall Street dragged the German share market down in early trade. When the Dow Jones again opened lower, German equities again took a hammering.
"There is no major demand out there, no major figures from the states, maybe it's just a case of people getting caught on the wrong side. The futures market is also having a big influence," he said.
Dealers also said that the futures market was putting pressure on the share market.
The focus over most of the day was on financials, particularly the banks as takeover speculation continued with talk of a possible takeover by HSBC of Commerzbank.
Commerzbank led volumes for most of the day, trading ahead against the trend at 66 marks, up 2.05 marks or 3.21 percent.
Dealers said they did not give the talk much credence, but said the rumours were supporting interest in the bank, long identified as a potential takeover candidate.
Deutsche Bank AG was also heavily traded but came off early gains to stand at 119.30 marks, down 1.20 marks.
For the next week, dealers were looking ahead to a rash of interim figures from the German chemical companies, including Henkel on Tuesday, Hoechst on Wednesday and BASF on Thursday.
